verdicts.title: Add a validate_endianness helper and reject typo'd endianness at BitType construction and bytes_to_bittype
verdicts.issues: No substantive problems; all claims re-verified empirically. Before-code matches pristine source exactly (utils.py imports, bittype.py 21/148-151/621-625). Placement claim probed and confirmed: validation after source_else_big resolution catches EVERY constructor path -- UInt16/SInt16 (int.py forwards to base, no edit needed), Float32, Buffer.specialize, UTF8String.specialize (String has no own __init__; BitType.__init__ is the only one besides SInt's forwarding one), UInt.specialize/SInt.specialize classes, bits=... path, endianness=None (rejected), explicit 'source_else_big' (still resolves to 'big'), copy-construction from a little-endian box (propagates 'little'). specialize() takes no endianness so no class-level default can bypass; the endianness property has no setter; pickle round-trips already-validated state. Deliberate non-patch of BitVector.to_int verified on ALL THREE backends (native, speedup, bitarray -- bitarray is the active one): int.from_bytes raises ValueError "byteorder must be either 'little' or 'big'" for bad strings, including on empty vectors; from_bytes/to_bytes take a reverse_endianness bool, not a string. Inconsistent-fallback BEFORE evidence reproduced on pristine code: constructor typo -> little (b'\x02\x01'), bytes_to_bittype typo -> big. Happy paths byte-identical before/after. Full suite on patched copy: 854/854, import path confirmed via bytemaker.__file__ from neutral cwd. Nit only: validate_endianness on bytes_to_bittype runs per-field on the plan.parse hot path (double validation), acknowledged in the proposal and negligible. CAUTION for any empirical re-verification: running python from the repo root puts the pristine repo ahead of PYTHONPATH (cwd precedes it) -- I initially got a false 'String path not validated' result this way; always verify bytemaker.__file__.

verdicts.title: Validate endianness at every conversion, aggregate, oracle, and schema intake (pytypes, ctypes, legacy aggregate, wrappers, Array)
verdicts.issues: No substantive problems; site completeness, oracle sync, and composition all independently re-verified. Own grep sweep over the package (endianness/endian/byteorder, incl. fields.py, fields.pyi, plans.py, bitvector backends, __init__.py): the 14 claimed sites are the complete set of string intakes; fields.py/.pyi have none; Struct.parse/pack and Array.parse/pack take no per-call endianness (compiled per class, validated at StructMeta/Array intake); package-exported Plan has no endianness-taking methods; the endianness-taking LegacyRecordPlan.parse/pack (plans.py 499/514) are called ONLY from the two validated aggregate_types entries (grep-confirmed), matching the 'validated transitively' claim -- note-level residue: LegacyRecordPlan.pack itself still falls back to big for a typo if someone imports that internal class directly, and Array.of with an unhashable endian raises TypeError from the cache-key lookup before PlanCompileError (silly input, cosmetic). Oracle sync verified structurally and empirically: aggregate_types re-exports to_bytes_individual/from_bytes_individual verbatim (confirmed same function objects via 'is'), and the aggregate pair raises the IDENTICAL ValueError message from both the public wrapper and a direct legacy.* call (message equality tested); valid-input parity byte-identical; plan_fastpath differential tests green. All BEFORE fallback directions reproduced on pristine code exactly as tabulated (pytypes typo->big, ctypes typo->reverse-of-host, legacy individual/aggregate typo->big, Array typo->big, StructMeta already loud). AFTER: every intake raises with the claimed message and exception type (ValueError at conversions/aggregates, PlanCompileError naming 'Array endian'/'S: endian' at schema sites); exc= parameterization correct at each site; endian=None inherit sentinel preserved (validated only when not None). Happy paths byte-identical incl. Array endian-unset. Full suite 854/854 on the endianness-only copy AND on a combined copy with ctypes-1(+elem_size==0 amendment)/2/3 and pytypes-1/2/3 applied on top; all compose anchors matched cleanly in that order, head insertions survived the reverse_ctype_endianness rewrite (grep-confirmed post-compose), and combined probes pass (caller non-mutation + typo rejection + spaced TypeError all coexist). Two nits, no action required: (1) pytype_to_bytes/bytes_to_pytype validate at first USE (inside the reversal test) rather than at body head like the ctypes/aggregate sites, so a value error can mask the endianness error -- e.g. with pytypes-3 applied, pytype_to_bytes('ABC','litle') raises the char-codec ValueError, not the endianness one; still loud, never silent-wrong. (2) Reverse compose order (ctypes-3 first) requires re-anchoring the ctype_to_bytes/bytes_to_ctype insertions because endianness-2's 'after' snippet shows the guard with the pristine (unspaced) message; the proposal itself flags this and the insertion is a bare head statement, so it is only a literal-patch hazard, not a semantic one.
